title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act s. 15 — Statutory provision (ACA s. 15)

content.overview: Section 15 deals with termination of an arbitrator's mandate for reasons other than those in section 13(2), including withdrawal, agreement and other statutory termination, and provides for appointment of a substitute arbitrator.
content.glance: Section 15 deals with termination of an arbitrator's mandate for reasons other than those in section 13(2), including withdrawal, agreement and other statutory termination, and provides for appointment of a substitute arbitrator.
content.study:
Section 15 — Termination and substitution

Apart from the situations addressed by section 13(2), an arbitrator's mandate terminates where the arbitrator withdraws or the parties agree to termination, and in the other cases recognised by the Act.

A substitute arbitrator is appointed according to the rules that were applicable to the appointment of the arbitrator being replaced. The Act further provides that, unless the parties agree otherwise, the reconstituted tribunal may continue from the stage already reached rather than automatically recommencing the proceedings.

provisions.title: Termination of mandate and substitution of arbitrator

examples.title: Application 1
examples.body: An arbitrator withdraws with the circumstances contemplated by the Act; a substitute is appointed using the appointment rules applicable to the original appointment.

examples.title: Application 2
examples.body: A substitute enters after pleadings and evidence have progressed; the tribunal considers continuation from the existing stage under section 15.
